title: Resilient Industrial Sensor Aggregation
business: Manufacturing firms managing thousands of distributed IoT sensors across factory floors.
problem: Traditional monolithic architectures suffer from cascading failures when a single sensor node crashes, leading to data loss and expensive downtime for the entire production line.
solution: Elixir leverages the BEAM virtual machine to isolate sensor processes. By using immutable data structures and supervision trees, the system ensures that if one sensor process encounters an error, it is automatically restarted without affecting the rest of the network, maintaining high availability.
steps: Define a supervisor process to manage individual sensor worker processes.
Implement sensor logic as isolated processes that handle incoming data streams.
Utilize immutable data structures to pass sensor readings between processes without risk of side effects.
Configure supervision strategies to restart failed sensor processes automatically.
Connect distributed nodes across the factory floor using Erlang distribution to aggregate data centrally.
outcome: A self-healing system where individual sensor failures are contained and recovered instantly, ensuring continuous data flow.
limitation: The overhead of process isolation and message passing can increase latency compared to shared-memory models; verify this by monitoring process mailbox sizes and mailbox latency under peak load.
